review.reason: Candidate 35 passes as supplied. Hole 1 is a 192-yard punchbowl par 3 with a substantial lake left and forward of the green. The clear line away from the water is supported by all nine tee-dispersion probes finishing safely; challenging the hazard-side line adds some risk, making this a relatively accessible opener. Hole 2 is a 157-yard island-green par 3. Its lake makes the carry the round’s most exacting target, while six of nine dispersion probes remain playable, so it is demanding without appearing to require a single perfect shot. Hole 3 is a dry 555-yard three-shot par 5 with a broad staged route and five bunkers. Only three of nine tee-dispersion probes finish safely, but all remain playable, offering a more demanding finish with recoverable misses and a choice between measured progress and pressing forward. The two par 3s use different target geometries and hazard demands, followed by a long positional hole; despite sharing a 3-wood tee club on the par 3s, the round has useful internal contrast. Recent rounds often use par-3/5/4 or par-5/3/4 sequences, while this par-3/3/5 set and its single island carry provide sufficient freshness. The current geometry balances an approachable start, a demanding carry, and a staged par-5 finish. No edits are needed.
